title: Arithmetic Progressions
summary: A list of numbers in which each term after the first is obtained by adding the same fixed number to the term before it is an arithmetic progression (A.P.). The first term is a and the fixed number is the common difference d = (any term) − (the term before it); d can be positive, negative or zero. 6, 7, 8, 9, … (d = 1), 10, 5, 0, −5, … (d = −5) and 2, 2, 2, … (d = 0) are A.P.s; 3, 7, 12, 18, … is not, because the differences 4, 5, 6 are not equal.

Three numbers a, b, c are in A.P. when b − a = c − b, i.e. 2b = a + c (the middle term is the average of the other two). So if 2p + 1, 13, 5p − 3 are in A.P., 26 = 7p − 2 and p = 4. When three terms of an A.P. must be found from their sum, take them as a − d, a, a + d.

aₙ = a + (n − 1)d. Example: in −3, 4, 11, …, a = −3, d = 7, so a₂₁ = −3 + 20 × 7 = 137. To find how many terms a finite A.P. has, put the last term l = a + (n − 1)d and solve for n. The nth term from the end of an A.P. with last term l is l − (n − 1)d: the 9th term from the end of 7, 11, …, 147 is 147 − 8 × 4 = 115.

Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d], or Sₙ = n/2 (a + l) when the last term l is known. The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n + 1)/2 and of the first n odd numbers is n². If Sₙ is given, form the equation and solve for n (it may be quadratic; reject negative or fractional n). The nth term can also be found as aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁.

Rows of plants decreasing by 2 in each row, prizes each ₹20 less than the one before, savings increasing by a fixed amount, and numbers leaving a fixed remainder on division (2-digit numbers leaving remainder 1 when divided by 4 are 13, 17, …, 97) all form A.P.s.
mcq: If 2p + 1, 13 and 5p − 3 are in A.P., then p is —

mcq.work:
In an A.P. the middle term is the average: 2 × 13 = (2p + 1) + (5p − 3).
26 = 7p − 2 ⇒ 7p = 28 ⇒ p = 4.

mcq: The 9th term from the end of the A.P. 7, 11, 15, …, 147 is —

mcq.work:
d = 11 − 7 = 4 and the last term l = 147.
Counting from the end, the terms go down by 4: nth term from the end = l − (n − 1)d.
9th from the end = 147 − 8 × 4 = 147 − 32 = 115.

mcq: Three numbers in A.P. have sum 18 and product 120. They are —

mcq.work:
Take the numbers as a − d, a, a + d. Sum 3a = 18 ⇒ a = 6.
Product (6 − d)(6)(6 + d) = 120 ⇒ 36 − d² = 20 ⇒ d² = 16 ⇒ d = 4.
The numbers are 2, 6, 10.

mcq: If x + 2, 2x + 5 and 4x + 8 are in A.P., x is —

mcq.work:
2(2x + 5) = (x + 2) + (4x + 8) ⇒ 4x + 10 = 5x + 10 ⇒ x = 0.
The terms are 2, 5, 8 — common difference 3 ✓.

mcq: The number of terms in the A.P. 3, 17, 31, …, 101 is —
Which of the following is an A.P.?

mcq.work:
Check the differences:
6, 7, 8, 9, 10: 1, 1, 1, 1 — equal, so an A.P.
−5, −1, 3, 8: 4, 4, 5 — not equal. a, a + b, a + 2b, a + 4b: b, b, 2b — not equal. 3, 7, 12, 18: 4, 5, 6 — not equal.

mcq: An A.P. has sum of first three terms 18 and common difference 4. The A.P. is —

mcq.work:
First three terms: a, a + 4, a + 8. Sum 3a + 12 = 18 ⇒ a = 2.
The A.P. is 2, 6, 10, …

mcq: The common difference of the A.P. 10, 5, 0, −5, … is —
The sum of the first 20 odd natural numbers is —

mcq.work:
1, 3, 5, … : a = 1, d = 2, n = 20.
S₂₀ = 20/2 [2 + 19 × 2] = 10 × 40 = 400. (In general the sum of the first n odd numbers is n².)

vsa: For an A.P. with a = −2 and d = 5, find the 10th term and the sum of the first 10 terms.

or: The 5th term of an A.P. is 23 and the 12th term is 37. Find a and d.

a + 4d = 23 and a + 11d = 37.
Subtract: 7d = 14 ⇒ d = 2. Then a = 23 − 8 = 15.
